newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares in sharp rally in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares in sharp rally in late trade.

text.p: Bombay blue chips added onto early gains in late Wednesday trade due to continued fund buying and restricted supply in front-line stocks, traders said.
"The rally is now taking place across-the-board," said Purvesh Shah, chief dealer at Nuclues Securities. "Fund buying has improved market sentiments and there is little supply seen at higher levels."
The market's blistering rally brought Bombay's top share index within striking distance of the psychological 4,000 level.
At 1445 p.m. (0915 GMT), Bombay's benchmark 30-share index was up 75.50 points, or 1.96 percent, at 3,936.47, the day's highest level.
Software, oil and refinery and multinational stocks continued to top the shopping list of foreign funds, players said.
"There has been a decent amount of buying by funds and the sectoral focus continues," said the dealing head at a foreign brokerage.
Oil, refineries and software stocks attracted buying interest ahead of an anticipated increaes in prices of domestic petroleum products on June 15, players said.
"These stocks won't be directly affected by the petroleum price hike and so to an extent, funds are hedging their risks," said Nucleus' Shah.
Shares at the National Stock Exchange rode higher on the first day of the weekly account, prompting operators to build up fresh market positions.

Huge auctions in front-line stocks such as tobacco giant, ITC (116,000 shares), petrochemical major Reliance Industries (60,000 shares) and some other stocks also contributed to the market's sharp rally, traders said.
"The huge auctions show that people have been going short in the market and so bull operators will now try to trap bears," said Manish Nathwani, dealer at brokers Samir Doshi.
Heavy selling by operators who do not have actual delivery of the shares leads to the stocks being auctioned at higher prices, traders said.

Local mutual funds showed hesitancy to sell stocks in a rising market, thus helping the market rally further, participants said. Heavy buying couple with restricted supply in blue chip shares was thus stoking an upward trend, they said.
